propositions: Ticking an AC checkbox does not invalidate a plan-review attestation because checkbox state is normalized out before hashing by _normalize_checkbox_state, but the fixed staleness message lists 'description/AC/file_impact/children' as if AC is a basis component, making it impossible to determine which input actually changed.

The material fingerprint basis consists of exactly four keys (ticket_id, description, file_impact, children) plus file_impact_scope when scope is none, but staleness messages incorrectly name a non-existent AC component and cannot distinguish a tick-only edit from no edit.

Pre-330c attestations hashed the raw description without checkbox normalization, so after ticking a checkbox the normalized recompute and legacy grandfather cannot match, producing a spurious stale-material verdict with no component actually edited.

Per-component fingerprints must be signed in the manifest rather than reconstructed at read time because children is derived from other tickets' state at read time and could diverge from what the reviewer saw.

Every attestation refusal surface must name which component(s) changed or plainly state that no component difference can be named, and related surfaces like stale-reopened and signing failures must provide similarly actionable remedies.
